brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A baked green tea from Yong'an in Fujian, also called Yunfeng Qingming.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
name_ru: Юн Ань Юнь Фэн Мао Фэн
history: It was developed in 1978 from downy Fuyun-line bushes and the early, fragrant Huangdan variety. It is graded in three levels and sold mainly in Jiangsu and Shanghai. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Spread to cool, fixed quickly at high heat, rolled lightly to keep the down, then baked in thin layers.
harvest_season: Between Jingzhe and Qingming, one bud with one or two leaves.
appearance_dry: Tight, straight, bright green strands rich in white down.
taste_profile: Fresh and mellow, with a refined aroma.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
